newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Turnover lower, volume thin on Bucharest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Turnover lower, volume thin on Bucharest bourse.

text.p: Turnover on the Bucharest stock exchange fell sharply on Tuesday to 58.7 million lei or one fourth of its previous level.
"Buying interest from retail investors, who still dominate trading, was light today," a broker said.

Fertiliser maker Azomures SA stayed in the limelight, snatching 52 percent of turnover. But traders said interest in the company had been on the slide on Tuesday sending prices lower to 12,800 lei from 14,200.
"There was heavy buying in Azomures for a while after release of fine half-year results but demand was low today," another broker said.
Demand outran supply for eight of the 13 traded stocks pushing prices up. Three stocks fell, one stayed flat and one had no trade.
Investors also centered on Artrom SA engineering company, in which 5,512 of the 10,043 traded shares changed hands. Artrom closed 50 lei stronger at 2,650 lei.
But traders said Artrom could not influence the level of turnover due to its low prices.

The U.S. missile attack on Iraq had no impact on Bucharest trading and brokers shrugged off any influence in the future. "This market has a hard time reacting to news about its own stocks, let alone international news," said a broker.

The unofficial VAB Index -- a value-weighted index of all stocks computed by Vanguard SA securities -- was 2.9 percent down from the previous session, closing at 373 points. Its base was 1,000 points when it was created last November.
